description: es un equipo de estudiantes de Ingeniería en Sistemas Computacionales que busca transformar datos de la NASA en soluciones inteligentes para el campo. A través de tecnología, análisis de datos e inteligencia artificial, desarrollamos herramientas que ayuden a los agricultores a tomar mejores decisiones y adaptar sus cultivos frente a los desafíos climáticos.
summary:
What was developed?
We developed AgroStake, a comprehensive agricultural monitoring system that combines an IoT smart stake (based on ESP32) with an interactive web platform for real-time soil diagnostics.

How does it address the challenge?
The system fuses local root-level telemetry data (temperature, capacitive moisture, and pH) with satellite climate information obtained through the NASA POWER API (MERRA-2 precipitation). AgroStake processes these combined environmental metrics using FAO-56 agronomic standards and a viability algorithm, successfully recommending the most suitable crops for that plot and generating care alerts (irrigation, acidity).

Why is it important?
It is vital because it democratizes precision agriculture. By connecting NASA's spatial data with the land of local producers, AgroStake empowers farmers to optimize water usage, adapt their crops to climate variability, and sustainably protect food security.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? AgroStake is a comprehensive IoT agricultural monitoring system. It operates through a smart physical stake inserted into the crop area to measure temperature and moisture directly at the root level. This data is transmitted via Wi-Fi or Bluetooth to a web platform, where it is cross-referenced in real time with satellite precipitation data from NASA POWER and pH levels. The system uses the FAO-56 agronomic standard to evaluate these 4 variables and determine which crops from the catalog are most viable to plant.

What benefits does it have?

  • Informed decisions: Eliminates "blind" planting by indicating exactly which crop has the highest probability of success based on daily conditions.
  • Resource optimization: Generates automated alerts indicating when it is actually necessary to irrigate or adjust soil pH.
  • Accessibility: Translates complex agronomic data into a clean, easy-to-understand visual format, supported by an Artificial Intelligence Assistant that responds in natural language.

What is the intended impact of the project? The main objective is to democratize precision agriculture. By facilitating access to the fusion of satellite data (NASA) and local sensors, we aim to protect crop yields, promote water conservation, and ensure food security in the face of current climate variability.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Hardware: ESP32-C3 microcontroller, DS18B20 temperature sensor, and capacitive soil moisture sensor.
  • Software (Frontend): Built with React and TypeScript, bundled with Vite, and styled with Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend and Data: Relational architecture in PostgreSQL v3.3, integration of the NASA POWER satellite API (MERRA-2 product), and use of MQTT and BLE communication protocols.

How is your project creative? AgroStake's innovation lies in connecting two worlds: physical micro-readings centimeters underground with NASA's spatial macro-telemetry. Furthermore, it breaks away from interfaces cluttered with raw data; its web design is intentionally clean and minimalist, using an algorithm (AI Score) that rates crop viability from 0 to 100%, making data science accessible to any user.

What factors did your team consider? We primarily considered intermittent connectivity in rural areas, equipping the stake with dual connectivity (Wi-Fi for areas with network coverage and Bluetooth BLE for direct offline syncing to a mobile phone). We also accounted for farmers' learning curves, prioritizing a high-contrast interface design and step-by-step guided menus to prevent technological frustration.
